  FILE 55/229: src/app/api/discussions/route.js
  Score: 7/100   Issues: 10

  The discussions API stores all thread data inside the tenant's JSONB `settings` column, which will cause unbounded growth, race conditions, and data loss under concurrent writes. The `nowLabel()` function returns a static string 'Just now' instead of a real timestamp, making the 'lastActivity' field useless for sorting or display. There is no input sanitization for thread content, no pagination, and no database-level isolation for the read-modify-write pattern in POST and PATCH. The biggest risk is data corruption and loss when multiple users reply simultaneously.

  [HIGH] bug -- Line 6
  nowLabel() returns a static string 'Just now' instead of an actual timestamp. This makes the 'lastActivity' field meaningless for sorting, filtering, or displaying relative time. Threads will always appear equally recent.
  Fix: Return an ISO 8601 timestamp (e.g., new Date().toISOString()) and compute relative time on the client side.

  [HIGH] bug -- Line 74
  Thread ID is generated using Date.now() which is not unique under high concurrency. Two threads created in the same millisecond will have the same ID, causing data loss.
  Fix: Use a cryptographically random ID (e.g., crypto.randomUUID()) or a combination of timestamp + random suffix.

  [CRITICAL] concurrency -- Line 72
  POST handler performs a read-modify-write on tenant settings without any locking or transaction isolation. Two concurrent POST requests will both load the same threads array, each prepend their new thread, and the second write will overwrite the first, causing data loss.
  Fix: Use a database transaction with SELECT FOR UPDATE on the tenants row, or use a JSONB append operation (e.g., jsonb_set) to atomically prepend the new thread.

  [CRITICAL] concurrency -- Line 117
  PATCH handler has the same race condition as POST. Two concurrent replies to the same thread will both load the same replies array, each append their reply, and the second write will overwrite the first, losing one reply.
  Fix: Use the same SELECT FOR UPDATE transaction pattern as POST, or use a JSONB path update to atomically append to the replies array.

  [HIGH] security -- Line 65
  No sanitization or length validation on topic, company, campus, or text fields. An attacker can inject arbitrary JSON, HTML, or extremely long strings, leading to XSS in the frontend or database storage abuse.
  Fix: Strip HTML tags, enforce maximum lengths (e.g., topic max 200 chars, text max 5000 chars), and validate against allowed character patterns.

  [MEDIUM] performance -- Line 47
  All threads are loaded into memory and returned in a single response. As the number of threads grows, this will cause high memory usage and slow responses. There is no pagination or limit.
  Fix: Implement pagination using query parameters (page, limit) and slice the threads array server-side.

  [MEDIUM] error_handling -- Line 43
  If the tenant is not found, the API returns an empty threads array with a 200 status. This could mask configuration errors or invalid tenant IDs. A 404 status would be more appropriate.
  Fix: Return a 404 status when the tenant is not found, unless the caller explicitly expects an empty result.

  [MEDIUM] multi_tenancy -- Line 25
  resolveTenantId allows any role to pass a campusId query parameter, which could let an employer or super_admin access discussions of any tenant by guessing or enumerating tenant IDs. There is no check that the employer belongs to that tenant.
  Fix: For employer role, validate that the employer's tenant_id matches the requested campusId, or restrict to session tenant only.

  [LOW] data_integrity -- Line 84
  Reply 'role' is derived from session.user.role, but the mapping is incomplete: 'super_admin' is not mapped, so it will fall through to 'company' which is misleading.
  Fix: Add a mapping for super_admin or default to 'admin'.

  [MEDIUM] observability -- Line 50
  Error logging uses console.error with a generic prefix but does not include the tenantId or any correlation ID, making it difficult to debug issues in production.

  FILE 88/229: src/app/api/student/offers/route.js
  Score: 68/100   Issues: 10

  The offers API has a critical race condition in the GET endpoint where auto-expiry updates are performed sequentially without a transaction, risking partial updates and inconsistent state under concurrent access. The PATCH endpoint lacks input validation for the offer ID format and does not handle the case where a student accepts an offer while another is already accepted, which could lead to duplicate accepted offers. The error messages are generic and not actionable. Overall, the code is functional but has reliability and data integrity risks that need addressing before production deployment.

  [HIGH] concurrency -- Line 36
  Race condition in auto-expiry loop: multiple concurrent GET requests can simultaneously read pending offers, both detect expiry, and both attempt UPDATE. Without a transaction or SELECT FOR UPDATE, the same offer may be updated multiple times, and the loop modifies the in-memory object while iterating, which is safe but the DB updates are not atomic with the read. This can lead to inconsistent state if a PATCH request arrives between the read and the update.
  Fix: Wrap the read and update in a database transaction with SELECT FOR UPDATE to lock the rows, or move auto-expiry to a scheduled background job instead of doing it on every GET request.

  [HIGH] business_logic -- Line 80
  The PATCH endpoint does not check if the student already has an accepted offer before accepting a new one. A student could accept multiple offers by sending concurrent PATCH requests, violating the business rule that a student should only have one accepted offer.
  Fix: Add a check before the UPDATE to ensure the student does not already have an accepted offer. Use a transaction to atomically check and update.

  [MEDIUM] validation -- Line 73
  The offer ID is not validated as a UUID before being used in the query. If a malformed ID is passed, the query will fail with a database error (invalid input syntax for type uuid), resulting in a 500 error instead of a 400. This also opens a potential for SQL injection if the input is not properly sanitized, though parameterized queries mitigate that risk.
  Fix: Validate that the id is a valid UUID using a regex or a library like uuid.validate() before using it in the query.

  [MEDIUM] logic -- Line 79
  The status mapping uses 'declined' but the database CHECK constraint for offers.status only allows 'rejected', not 'declined'. This will cause a database constraint violation error when a student declines an offer.
  Fix: Change 'declined' to 'rejected' to match the database schema, or update the schema to include 'declined' if that is the intended status.

  [LOW] ux_copy -- Line 52
  Error message 'Failed to load student offers' is generic and not actionable for the user. It does not indicate what went wrong or what the user can do.
  Fix: Provide a more specific error message, e.g., 'Unable to load your offers. Please try again later.' and log the detailed error server-side.

  [LOW] ux_copy -- Line 96
  Error message 'Failed to update offer status' is generic and not actionable. It does not tell the user what happened or what to do next.
  Fix: Provide a more specific error message, e.g., 'Unable to update offer status. Please try again later.' and log the detailed error server-side.

  [LOW] authentication -- Line 9
  The role check uses 'student' but the database schema defines the role as 'student' in the users table. This is correct, but the error message 'Unauthorized' is generic and does not indicate whether the user is not logged in or does not have the correct role.
  Fix: Differentiate between 'not authenticated' (401) and 'forbidden' (403) with appropriate messages.

  [LOW] authentication -- Line 63
  Same generic 'Unauthorized' error in PATCH endpoint. Should differentiate between 401 and 403.
  Fix: Same fix as GET endpoint.

  [LOW] performance -- Line 33
  Auto-expiry logic runs on every GET request, performing N sequential UPDATE queries for expired offers. This is inefficient and does not scale. For a student with many expired offers, this could cause noticeable latency.
  Fix: Move auto-expiry to a scheduled background job (e.g., cron) that runs periodically, or batch the updates into a single query.

  [LOW] error_handling -- Line 41
  The catch block in the auto-expiry loop silently logs the error but continues execution. If the UPDATE fails, the offer remains in 'pending' state in the database but is marked as 'expired' in the response, causing inconsistency between the returned data and the database.

  FILE 223/229: src/lib/studentServer.js

  [CRITICAL] concurrency -- Line 7
  Race condition in getOrCreateStudentProfileId: two concurrent calls for the same userId can both see no existing profile (line 8), both attempt INSERT (line 22-27), one succeeds, the other's INSERT is silently ignored by ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, then both re-query (line 29). The second caller gets the correct id, but the first caller's INSERT was silently dropped — if the first caller's transaction was rolled back or the connection failed after the INSERT, the profile is lost. This can cause data loss under concurrent load.
  Fix: Use a single INSERT ... ON CONFLICT ... RETURNING id query to atomically create or retrieve the profile in one round-trip, eliminating the race window.

  [HIGH] data_integrity -- Line 20

  Score: 0/100   Issues: 43

  The API route for student profiles is well-structured but has several critical issues, including a lack of authorization checks, silent defaulting of missing data, and exposure of internal error messages to the client. The DELETE endpoint has a critical data integrity issue, as it deletes the student_profiles record without cascading to related applications, offers, and user accounts, leaving orphaned records and inconsistent state. Additionally, the error handler exposes raw error messages to the client, which is a security concern, and there is a lack of input validation and CSRF protection. The code has a total of 43 issues, with 5 critical, 7 high, 22 medium, and 9 low severity issues, indicating a need for significant improvements to ensure security, data integrity, and reliability. Overall, while the code is generally well-structured, it requires substantial refinements to address the identified security and data integrity concerns.

  [CRITICAL] authorization -- Line 129
  DELETE endpoint only checks for a valid data-entry session (requireDataEntrySession) but does not verify that the authenticated user has the 'delete' permission or role. Any data-entry user can delete any student profile within their tenant, which is a privilege escalation vulnerability.
  Fix: Add an explicit role or permission check (e.g., requireRole('college_admin')) before allowing deletion, or restrict DELETE to specific user roles.

  [HIGH] data_integrity -- Line 112
  The PATCH endpoint defaults cgpa to 0 when it is not provided or is not a finite number (line 120: Number.isFinite(cgpa) ? cgpa : 0). This silently corrupts data by overwriting a student's actual CGPA with 0, which can affect eligibility calculations and reports.
  Fix: Require cgpa to be explicitly provided and validated; do not default to 0. Return a 400 error if cgpa is missing or invalid.

  [HIGH] security -- Line 125

  Fix: Log the full error server-side and return a generic error message to the client. Use a structured logging approach.

The code also lacks pagination, which could cause performance issues with large datasets, and the `getEmployerProfileId` function may return null without proper error handling, potentially causing downstream failures.

  FILE 97/229: src/app/dashboard/admin/feedback/page.js
  Score: 0/100   Issues: 26

  The `src/app/dashboard/admin/feedback/page.js` file has several critical, high, medium, and low issues, totaling 26, with 2 critical, 6 high, 10 medium, and 8 low issues. The feedback inbox page has a critical multi-tenancy vulnerability, lacking proper filtering by the admin's tenant_id, and other issues include the lack of optimistic UI updates, error rollback, and pagination. The feedback management UI component lacks input validation on the reply textarea, which could allow XSS injection, and has other issues such as missing confirmation dialogs for destructive status changes and character limits on the reply textarea. Additionally, various code snippets show a lack of error handling and user feedback for the sendReply function, potential race conditions, and missing accessibility attributes. Overall, the file requires significant improvements to address security, data integrity, and user experience concerns.

  [CRITICAL] multi_tenancy -- Line 18
  The SWR fetcher calls `/api/feedback` without any tenant_id filter. If the backend does not enforce tenant isolation, this endpoint will return feedback from ALL tenants, causing cross-tenant data leakage. The admin's tenant_id must be passed as a query parameter or enforced server-side via session.
  Fix: Add tenant_id query parameter to the fetch URL, e.g., `/api/feedback?tenant_id=${session.user.tenantId}`, and ensure the backend validates it against the authenticated user's tenant.

  [HIGH] edge_case -- Line 25
  If `data` is null or undefined (e.g., API returns 200 with no body), `data?.items || []` will default to an empty array, but the code does not handle the case where `data` is an unexpected shape (e.g., `{ feedback: [] }` instead of `{ items: [] }`). This will cause a silent empty state with no error feedback.
  Fix: Add validation for the API response shape and show a meaningful error if the structure is unexpected.

  [HIGH] uiux -- Line 34
  The `updateStatus` function does not provide optimistic UI updates. When the user changes the status dropdown, the UI will not reflect the change until `mutate()` re-fetches the entire list, causing a noticeable delay and poor UX. Additionally, if the API fails, the dropdown will revert to the old value without warning.
  Fix: Implement optimistic update: immediately update the local state, then revert on API failure.

  [HIGH] concurrency -- Line 82
  `Promise.all([mutate(), openThread(selectedId)])` has a race condition: `mutate()` re-fetches the entire feedback list, while `openThread` also fetches the thread data. If `mutate` completes before `openThread`, the thread data may be stale. More critically, `openThread` sets `setThreadLoading(true)` which could cause a flash of loading state after the reply is already posted.
  Fix: Call `mutate()` first, then `openThread` in sequence, or use `mutate`'s revalidation option to avoid double fetch.

  [MEDIUM] performance -- Line 148
  The entire feedback list is rendered without pagination. As the number of feedback items grows (potentially thousands), this will cause significant DOM rendering overhead and slow page load. The API endpoint likely returns all items without pagination.
  Fix: Implement server-side pagination with page size (e.g., 50 items) and add a 'Load More' button or infinite scroll.

  [MEDIUM] security -- Line 159

  fetcher function on line 8 does not check response.ok before calling r.json(). If the API returns a non-2xx status (e.g., 500, 404), r.json() will still attempt to parse the error body, but the promise will resolve without throwing, causing SWR to treat the error response as successful data. This can lead to silent data corruption or crashes when the malformed data is used downstream.

  The student management page is generally well-structured with proper loading, error, and empty states, but it has several critical issues including missing pagination for large datasets, silent error handling in CSV import catch blocks, and potential null pointer exceptions when accessing nested student properties. The biggest risks are the lack of tenant isolation in data queries, which could lead to cross-tenant data leakage, and unhandled promise rejections from CSV parsing utilities that may crash the application on malformed input. While the component correctly scopes data to the current tenant and uses centralized CSV utilities, the absence of input sanitization and error boundaries around CSV operations poses security vulnerabilities. Overall, the code requires pagination, robust error handling, and proper null checks before production deployment.

Error handling is minimal, with no distinction between network and API errors, potential crashes from non-JSON responses, and generic success messages that don't confirm which offer was affected. The code lacks input validation before API calls, loading states for destructive operations, and proper null checks on nested objects, risking data integrity issues and runtime crashes. Overall, the component requires immediate security hardening, robust error handling, and production-grade user feedback before deployment.

  Fix: Add a check for response content-type before calling json(), or wrap json() calls in try-catch.

  [CRITICAL] input_validation -- Line 100

  Fix: Check response content-type before parsing JSON, or use text() and parse manually.

  The user management page has critical security vulnerabilities: passwords are sent and stored in plaintext, and the delete endpoint lacks server-side authorization, allowing any authenticated user to delete any user by ID (IDOR) and is vulnerable to CSRF attacks. The code also lacks client-side validation for required fields, uses a vague browser confirm() dialog for destructive actions, and has weak error handling that may expose internal details or crash on non-JSON responses. While the component is functional with basic loading states, it requires production-grade safeguards including proper authentication, input sanitization, and accessible error/success messaging.

  [CRITICAL] security -- Line 10

  FILE 202/229: src/lib/csvExport.js
  Score: 82/100   Issues: 5

  The CSV export module is generally well-structured with proper RFC 4180 escaping and BOM handling. The main risks are: (1) the `parseCsv` function has a bug where trailing empty fields at the end of a line are lost due to the `row.some` filter, causing data corruption for rows ending with empty cells; (2) the parser does not handle carriage return (`\r`) as a line terminator, which can cause malformed parsing on Windows-generated CSV files; (3) the `downloadCsv` function creates a blob URL but does not handle potential memory leaks if called rapidly in a loop. Overall, the code is clean and functional for typical use cases.

  [HIGH] bug -- Line 79
  The filter `row.some((cell) => String(cell).trim() !== '')` on line 79 and 87 drops rows where all cells are empty strings, but also drops rows where the last cell(s) are empty. For example, a row 'a,b,' (three cells, last empty) will be parsed as ['a','b'] instead of ['a','b',''] because the empty trailing field is pushed but then the row is filtered out if all cells are empty after trimming. This causes data loss for rows ending with empty fields.
  Fix: Remove the row filtering logic that drops rows with all-empty cells, or apply it only to skip truly empty lines (e.g., blank lines between data). Instead, filter out empty lines before parsing or after building the full row array.

  [MEDIUM] bug -- Line 82
  The parser skips carriage return characters (`\r`) but does not treat `\r\n` as a single line terminator. On Windows-generated CSV files, lines end with `\r\n`. The current code will treat `\r` as a regular character (skipped) and then `\n` as a line break, which works for `\r\n` but will incorrectly handle `\r` alone (old Mac style) by ignoring it and not breaking the line. This can cause malformed parsing for files with `\r` line endings.
  Fix: Add handling for `\r` as a line terminator (either alone or as part of `\r\n`). Check if the next character is `\n` and skip it to avoid double line breaks.

  [MEDIUM] edge_case -- Line 79
  The filter `row.some((cell) => String(cell).trim() !== '')` on line 79 and 87 will drop rows that consist entirely of empty strings. While this is often desired to skip blank lines, it also drops rows that intentionally contain only empty cells (e.g., a placeholder row). This is a data integrity issue if the CSV is expected to preserve all rows.
  Fix: Consider removing the filter entirely or making it optional. If blank lines need to be skipped, filter them out before parsing or use a separate flag.

  [LOW] performance -- Line 30
  The `downloadCsv` function creates a Blob and an object URL for every download. If called rapidly in a loop (e.g., exporting many reports), this can cause memory pressure because `URL.revokeObjectURL` is called immediately after `click()`, but the browser may not have started the download yet. In some browsers, revoking the URL before the download starts can cause the download to fail.
  Fix: Consider using a small delay before revoking the URL, or use a different download approach (e.g., using a data URI with a link click). Alternatively, keep the URL alive until the download completes by listening to the `click` event and revoking after a timeout.

  [LOW] maintainability -- Line 52
  The `parseCsv` function is a manual state-machine parser that is moderately complex (40+ lines). It does not handle edge cases like fields with leading/trailing whitespace (which may be significant in some CSV dialects), or quoted fields spanning multiple lines (which is valid per RFC 4180). The function works for common cases but may fail on non-standard CSV inputs.
  Fix: Consider using a well-tested CSV parsing library (e.g., Papa Parse) for production use, or add more robust handling for multi-line quoted fields and whitespace trimming options.
